goal: Make Kolibri Factory enforce the owner rule that all 20 servers must stay working 24/7: Control Plane checks the factory, dispatches repair commands to agents, keeps fallback execution alive, classifies every canonical server, probes per-server MIMO/subagent capacity, and produces an owner-visible restore backlog.
objective: Run a remote read-mostly fleet guardian audit and design through Control Plane. Use Fabric API/Control Plane first and SSH only for bootstrap/diagnostics where already authorized. Do not do destructive repair. Produce exact artifacts that list all canonical servers, current working capacity, stale/duplicate cards, blockers, fallback routes, next repair tasks, 24/7 guardian loop, buddy-trigger handoff policy, target 20 MIMO/subagents per server capacity model, and 1000 logical-agent scheduler constraints.
verification_commands: GET Control Plane /v1/tasks for active P0 fleet tasks
classify fresh heartbeat <=15m, <=60m, stale, degraded and duplicate mesh cards
classify per-server MIMO/subagent capacity target and blockers
define 24/7 Control Plane guardian loop with task deduplication and backoff
verify exact required artifact files exist
acceptance: Remote execution happens on server/control node, not local Mac implementation.
All 20 canonical owner servers are listed or missing canonical identity is explicitly called out as blocker.
Fresh working capacity is counted separately from stale cards and mesh duplicates.
Every degraded/unreachable/stale canonical server has reason, fallback route and next repair task.
Control Plane guardian loop is specified as a 24/7 check/repair dispatcher.
Per-server target of up to 20 MIMO/subagents is capacity-gated, not assumed.
Logical agent scale up to 1000 is governed by scheduler limits and safety gates.
Buddy-trigger/handoff policy exists so healthy nodes continue checks and repairs.
No destructive commands, credential changes, firewall/VPN changes or production restarts are performed.
Owner-facing result states how many servers are fully working now and what must be repaired next.
